questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Develop a habit when getting in and out of your car. Before you start the car, fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead curves to the right and then to the left. Slow down so you can safely handle these curves.

questions.question: You should always use your turn signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. Signal when you pull into traffic from a parking space, change lanes, or pass another vehicle.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?

options.text: Road signs.
Pedestrians.
Other vehicles.
Street lights.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than road signs and other roadside objects.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:

options.text: Loss of focus.
Poor coordination.
Slower reaction time and judgment.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol harms your vision, judgment, focus, and coordination.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School ahead.
School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Construction workers on or near the road.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert drivers to dangers ahead. This sign warns that pedestrians may be crossing the road.

questions.question: You are entering a busy freeway. What should you do to merge safely?

options.text: Check your side mirrors, rearview mirror, and blind spots.
Use the on-ramp to speed up and match the freeway traffic speed.
Let traffic on the freeway go first.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic. Yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Before merging, check your mirrors and blind spots to make sure you have a safe space to enter.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Stop where you are.
Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, move safely to the right side of the road and stop. Create a clear path for the emergency vehicle. If you are in heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Is always a very safe driver.
Always has the right-of-way.
Should not let other cars pass.
May create a dangerous situation.

questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be unsafe. On a two-lane road where traffic is backing up behind you, pull over and let other vehicles pass. Only drive well under the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: A steady green light means you:

options.text: Must slow down and get ready to stop.
Must stop and look for oncoming traffic before going.
May go through the intersection if it is safe.
Cannot turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: May go through the intersection if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can drive through the intersection if the road is clear. You may also turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: A flagger directs you to stop.
A stop sign controls the crossing.
Flashing red signals and gates are present and working.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing if a flagger or stop sign directs you to. Also stop when flashing red signals and gates are present and working.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady green traffic light?

options.text: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: With a steady green light, yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and vehicles still in the intersection. You may continue, but drive at a speed where you can stop if the light changes before you reach it.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol at a social event, what helps ensure safe driving?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Get a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking 30 minutes before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: Arrange a ride home with a friend who does not drink. Coffee and cold showers cannot reduce blood alcohol or its effects. The body needs about one hour to eliminate alcohol from a single drink.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:

options.text: Flashing red light.
Steady yellow light.
Yellow arrow.
Flashing yellow light.

questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look both ways, and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What should you remember when driving on wet pavement?

options.text: Pavement is especially slippery right after rain starts.
Wet roads can cause hydroplaning.
Give yourself extra space to stop.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are dangerously slippery, especially right after it rains. Your tires travel on a thin layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down in heavy rain, standing water, or slush to prevent your wheels from losing grip.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for trucks.
Do not pass trucks.
Truck parking area ahead.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill is ahead.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: Larger blind spots.
Smaller blind spots.
No blind spots.
The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.explanation: The larger the vehicle, the larger its blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that cannot be seen in side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians only.
Intersection ahead.
Hiking trails ahead.
School crossing ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle approaching, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. Drive immediately to the right side of the road and stop until the vehicle passes. If you are in an intersection, pass through it first before stopping on the right side.

questions.question: Smoking and preparing to smoke while driving:

options.text: Do not affect driving abilities.
Help keep the driver alert.
Are distracting activities.
Are not distracting activities.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is a dangerous distraction. It causes you to take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in foggy weather?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Turn on your hazard lights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: You must use your headlights when you cannot see clearly for 500 feet or more. Use low beams, not high beams. High beams reflect light back into your eyes in fog or rain, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public road?

options.text: Yes, as long as you are not driving.
Yes, if you are in the back seat.
Yes, if you are in the back of a pickup truck.
No, never.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have open alcohol in a vehicle on any public road. This applies to all passengers and all areas of the vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Speed up.
Stop completely.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and look carefully before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and look carefully before proceeding.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of danger ahead. Slow down and be careful before you continue.

questions.question: Where are you not allowed to park?

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must park within 12 inches of the edge of the road.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving and judgment?

options.text: It helps your driving but hurts your judgment.
It hurts both your driving and your judgment.
It does not affect driving or judgment.
It does not affect judgment but it hurts driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: It hurts both your driving and your judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and makes it harder to see clearly. It also affects your ability to judge speed and distance, makes you more likely to take risks, and lowers your inhibitions.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the road mean?

options.text: Drivers from both directions can pass.
No one can pass.
You can pass if you are at the top of a hill.
You can pass during the day only.

questions.explanation: Yellow lines show that traffic is moving in opposite directions. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass, no matter which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a railroad gate that is moving up or down?

options.text: Yes, if a train is not too close.
Yes, if your vehicle can fit without hitting the gate.
Yes, if you look both ways first.
No, never.

questions.explanation: When lights are flashing, bells are ringing, or gates are moving at a railroad crossing, you must stop completely. Do not drive around or under a moving gate. Wait until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully raised before crossing.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on an interstate?

options.text: Stop and make a U-turn.
Get off at the next exit and go back to the one you missed.
Ask the driver next to you for help.
Back up on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and go back to the one you missed.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Drive to the next exit, turn around safely, and return to the exit you missed.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn into an exit. If you miss your exit, keep driving and take the next one.

questions.question: How should you safely cross railroad tracks?

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen and look both ways, then cross if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is coming.
Quickly drive under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen and look both ways, then cross if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Always listen for trains and look both ways before crossing the tracks. Watch for warning signals. Never cross until you are sure it is safe and no train is coming.
